areas.title: המאבק על הפוליטיקה, החברה והתרבות בעקבות המהפכות

units.title: המהפכה המדעית
units.syl: נושא 1 – נאורות: תפיסה חדשה של אדם וחברה
units.scope: Medieval/pre-modern view of knowledge (authority of Church, Aristotle, Ptolemy) vs. new inquiry method based on observation and experiment; Copernicus, Kepler, Galileo (telescope, trial 1633), Francis Bacon (induction/experiment), Descartes (doubt, reason), Newton (laws of motion, gravity, Principia 1687); scientific method; printing press and scientific societies (Royal Society); significance: confidence in human reason paving the way to the Enlightenment.

units.title: עקרונות הנאורות
units.syl: נושא 1 – נאורות: תפיסה חדשה של אדם וחברה
units.scope: 18th century Enlightenment: faith in reason, belief in progress, organising society on rational/scientific principles; natural rights (Locke: life, liberty, property), social contract (Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau), separation of powers (Montesquieu), religious tolerance and criticism of the Church (Voltaire), the Encyclopédie (Diderot), Kant 'Sapere aude'; decline of religion's centrality; enlightened absolutism briefly; spread via salons, coffee houses, print.

units.title: המהפכה האמריקנית
units.syl: נושא 1 – נאורות: תפיסה חדשה של אדם וחברה
units.scope: Thirteen colonies; causes (taxes after Seven Years' War, Stamp Act, 'no taxation without representation', Boston Tea Party 1773); war of independence 1775–1783; Declaration of Independence 4 July 1776 (Jefferson, natural rights, consent of governed, right to overthrow); Constitution 1787 (federalism, separation of powers, checks and balances); Bill of Rights 1791 (first 10 amendments: religion, speech, press); limits (slavery, women, Native Americans); applying Enlightenment principles to founding documents; influence on France.

units.title: החסידות והמתנגדים
units.syl: נושא 2 – היהודים בין רפורמה ונאורות (רשות, חלופה א׳)
units.scope: Background: Eastern European Jewry in the 18th century (Poland-Lithuania, crisis after 1648 Chmielnicki massacres and Sabbateanism, elitism of Torah scholarship); the Baal Shem Tov (Israel ben Eliezer, c.1700–1760) and his ideas: serving God in joy, devekut, prayer with kavana, worship in corporeality, value of the simple Jew; the tzaddik and the court; spread (the Maggid of Mezeritch); was Hasidism a 'reform movement'? Opposition: the Vilna Gaon (Rabbi Eliyahu, 1720–1797), the mitnagdim, the bans (herem 1772), reasons for opposition, Volozhin yeshiva (R. Chaim of Volozhin, 1803); outcome: reconciliation against the Haskalah.

units.title: השליטים הנאורים, ההשכלה והרפורמה הדתית
units.syl: נושא 2 – היהודים בין רפורמה ונאורות (רשות, חלופה ב׳)
units.scope: Enlightened absolutism and Jews: Joseph II's Edict of Tolerance (1782) – aims (productivisation, German language, schools) and Jewish responses; the Haskalah in Central Europe: Moses Mendelssohn (Bible translation to German, 'Jerusalem'), Naphtali Herz Wessely ('Divrei Shalom ve-Emet' 1782, Torat ha-Adam), Ha-Me'assef; religious reform: Abraham Geiger and Reform Judaism (changes in prayer, organ, sermon in German, Judaism as evolving), Samson Raphael Hirsch and Neo-Orthodoxy ('Torah im derech eretz'); traditional opposition: the Chatam Sofer (Rabbi Moshe Sofer, Pressburg, 'chadash assur min ha-Torah'); analysing reforms and why they provoked opposition.

units.title: המהפכה הצרפתית: קריסת המשטר הישן
units.scope: The Ancien Régime: absolute monarchy (Louis XVI), three estates and privileges, financial crisis, Enlightenment ideas, harvest failures; 1789: Estates-General (May), Tennis Court Oath, National Assembly, storming of the Bastille (14 July), Great Fear, abolition of feudalism (4 August), Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen (26 August), March on Versailles; constitution of 1791 (constitutional monarchy, separation of powers, active/passive citizens); slogan liberté, égalité, fraternité.

units.title: המהפכה הצרפתית: מרפובליקה לטרור
units.scope: Flight to Varennes 1791; war with Austria and Prussia 1792; storming of the Tuileries, end of monarchy, the Republic (September 1792), the Convention, Girondins vs Jacobins; execution of Louis XVI (January 1793); Committee of Public Safety, Robespierre, Reign of Terror 1793–94 (Law of Suspects, revolutionary tribunal, guillotine, Vendée), dechristianisation & revolutionary calendar; Thermidor (July 1794); the Directory 1795–1799; debate: was the Terror legitimate?

units.title: נפוליאון בונפרטה
units.scope: Rise: Toulon, Italian campaign, Egypt and Land of Israel campaign (1798–99, Acre); coup of 18 Brumaire (1799), Consulate, Emperor 1804; domestic reforms: Napoleonic Code (1804), centralised administration, Concordat with the Pope (1801), lycées, Bank of France; was he an heir to or betrayer of the Revolution; Napoleonic wars (Austerlitz 1805, Trafalgar 1805), Continental System, spread of revolutionary ideas in Europe and awakening nationalism; Russian campaign 1812 and defeat; Leipzig 1813, exile to Elba 1814, Hundred Days, Waterloo 1815, St Helena; Congress of Vienna 1815 and restoration. Suggested 'historical trial' of Napoleon.

units.title: היהודים במהפכה הצרפתית ובימי נפוליאון
units.scope: Jews in France before 1789 (Sephardim in Bordeaux/Bayonne, Ashkenazim in Alsace-Lorraine, the autonomous community – kehila); debate in the National Assembly (Clermont-Tonnerre 1789: 'To the Jews as a nation, nothing; to the Jews as individuals, everything'); emancipation of Sephardim (January 1790) and of all Jews (27 September 1791); meaning: individual equality vs end of communal autonomy; Napoleon and the Jews: Assembly of Jewish Notables (1806) and its 12 questions, the Grand Sanhedrin (1807), the consistories (1808), the 'Infamous Decree' (1808); spread of emancipation to conquered lands and its reversal after 1815; Jewish responses (supporters vs. those who feared assimilation).

units.title: אנגליה – חלוצת המהפכה התעשייתית
units.scope: What was the Industrial Revolution (from c.1760); why England first: agricultural revolution & enclosure of land, population growth, capital from trade and colonies, coal and iron, political stability, entrepreneurs; inventions: textile (flying shuttle, spinning jenny, water frame, power loom), James Watt's steam engine (1769/1776), iron, railways (Stephenson, Liverpool–Manchester 1830), steamships; shift from domestic/putting-out system to factory; division of labour; spread to Europe and USA.

units.title: השפעות המהפכה התעשייתית על היחיד והחברה
units.scope: Capitalism and free market (Adam Smith, The Wealth of Nations 1776, laissez-faire); urbanisation (Manchester), slums, sanitation, disease; geographic & social mobility; new classes: industrial bourgeoisie/capitalists and proletariat; working conditions: long hours, low wages, unsafe machines, women's and child labour; early responses: Luddites, Factory Acts (1833, 1847 Ten Hours Act); positive vs negative effects (rise in goods, transport, standard of living over time).

units.title: סוציאליזם, המאבק לצדק חברתי ואורח החיים הבורגני
units.scope: Socialism for social justice: utopian socialists (Robert Owen, New Lanark), Marx and Engels, The Communist Manifesto 1848 (class struggle, proletariat revolution, classless society); the workers' struggle: trade unions, strikes, workers' parties (e.g., British Labour, German SPD), the First International 1864, 1 May; reforms achieved; bourgeois life: values (work, thrift, education, respectability), family, home, separate spheres and women's status, leisure (holidays, theatre, cafés, sport); groups representing a workers' party or trade union presenting demands.

units.title: ליברליזם – רעיונות הנאורות במדינה המודרנית
units.scope: Restoration and the Congress of Vienna (Metternich, conservatism) as background; liberalism as adopting Enlightenment ideas: individual rights and freedoms (speech, press, religion, assembly, property), rule of law, constitution, limited government, equality before the law, free economy; liberal thinkers (John Stuart Mill 'On Liberty' 1859); liberal revolutions: 1830 (July Revolution), 1848 'Spring of Nations'; conservatism vs liberalism vs socialism comparison; analysing a 19th-century constitution.

units.title: התגבשות התודעה הלאומית
units.scope: What is a nation and modern nationalism; common elements: people, shared origin, language, territory, culture, heritage, history, and the will to self-determination; how the French Revolution and Napoleon spread national consciousness; romanticism, folk culture, national language and history (Herder, Brothers Grimm); civic vs ethnic nationalism; national movements: Greek independence (1821–1830), unification of Italy (Mazzini, Garibaldi, Cavour, 1861/1870), unification of Germany (Bismarck, 1871); influence on Jewish national consciousness (link forward to Zionism). Mention that nationalism is studied in depth in high school.

units.title: דמוקרטיזציה ופרלמנטריזם
units.scope: Democratisation: expanding the right to vote (Britain: Reform Acts 1832, 1867, 1884; France: universal male suffrage 1848), secret ballot (1872 UK), the Chartists (People's Charter 1838); strengthening parliaments, ministerial responsibility, parties; social legislation (Bismarck's social insurance 1880s, factory laws, compulsory education); women's suffrage struggle (suffragists/suffragettes, Emmeline Pankhurst; New Zealand 1893 first); Jews gaining political rights (e.g., Lionel de Rothschild in Parliament 1858); debate on extending voting rights to women, workers or Jews.

units.title: אמנות מודרנית כמבטאת שינוי תקופה: האימפרסיוניזם
units.scope: Academic art and the Salon vs. the Impressionists; Salon des Refusés (1863), first Impressionist exhibition 1874, the name from Monet 'Impression, Sunrise' (1872); characteristics: light and colour, outdoor painting (en plein air), visible brush strokes, everyday modern life (city, railways, leisure, cafés); artists: Monet, Renoir, Degas, Pissarro, Morisot; photography's invention (daguerreotype 1839) and its impact on painting; Japanese prints; how the art reflects the period (urbanisation, industry, bourgeois leisure, new technology like paint tubes and trains); how to analyse a painting. Describe paintings in words only (no images).

units.title: השתלבות היהודים באירופה: משכילים ומתבוללים
units.scope: Ways of Jewish integration in society, economy and culture in Western, Central and Eastern Europe in the 19th century: emancipation timeline (France 1791, Netherlands 1796, Britain 1858, Austria-Hungary 1867, Germany 1871; Russia none until 1917); urbanisation and moving to professions (banking, commerce, medicine, law, journalism, academia), the Rothschilds; acculturation vs assimilation vs conversion (Heinrich Heine 'entry ticket'); Haskalah in Eastern Europe (Russia: Pale of Settlement, cantonists under Nicholas I, reforms of Alexander II, Hebrew Haskalah, Yehuda Leib Gordon 'Be a man in the street and a Jew at home'); the identity of the Jewish individual in the nation-state: partnership vs alienation ('Germans of the Mosaic faith').

units.title: יהדות ארצות הברית: הגירה, קליטה וערבות
units.scope: Waves of Jewish immigration to the US: Sephardim (colonial period, New Amsterdam 1654), German Jews (1820–1880), mass immigration from Eastern Europe (1881–1914, ~2 million), Ellis Island; push and pull factors; life in New York's Lower East Side, sweatshops, Yiddish press (Forverts) and theatre, Jewish unions (ILGWU); absorption into American society and Americanisation, limits (discrimination, quotas later); American Jewry's involvement in European Jewry's fate and its limits (e.g., protests over Kishinev pogrom 1903, American Jewish Committee 1906, Joint/JDC 1914); suggested films 'Hester Street', 'An American Tail' (פייבל).

units.title: זרמים דתיים ביהדות והיחס לציונות
units.scope: Internal developments: religious streams of the 19th–early 20th century: Reform (Germany; in the US – Pittsburgh Platform 1885, Hebrew Union College), Orthodoxy (Neo-Orthodoxy of Hirsch; Haredi/ultra-orthodoxy, Chatam Sofer), Conservative/Positive-Historical (Zacharias Frankel; Jewish Theological Seminary, Solomon Schechter in US), secular Jewish identity; their relation to Zionism: early Reform rejection (Jews as religious group only), Haredi rejection (forcing the end, Agudat Yisrael 1912), Religious Zionism (Rabbis Kalischer and Alkalai as forerunners, Rabbi Reines, Mizrachi 1902, later Rav Kook), Conservative support; comparison table.

units.title: האנטישמיות המודרנית
units.scope: Traditional Christian Jew-hatred vs modern antisemitism: term coined by Wilhelm Marr (1879), racial theory, Social Darwinism, nationalism, economic crises (1873), conspiracy myths (later Protocols of the Elders of Zion), blood libels in the modern age (Damascus 1840, Tiszaeszlár 1882); manifestations: Central Europe – antisemitic parties (Stoecker, Karl Lueger mayor of Vienna 1897); Western Europe – France: Drumont, the Dreyfus Affair (1894–1906), Zola 'J'accuse' (1898); Eastern Europe – Russia: pogroms 1881–82 ('Storms in the Negev'), May Laws 1882, Kishinev pogrom 1903, state antisemitism; Jewish responses.

units.title: סולידריות יהודית בעידן המודרני
units.scope: Mutual responsibility ('Kol Yisrael arevim ze la-ze') in the modern age: the Damascus Affair (1840) and the intervention of Moses Montefiore and Adolphe Crémieux; the Mortara affair (1858); Alliance Israélite Universelle (כי״ח, founded Paris 1860 – defence of rights and a network of schools in Islamic lands, Mikveh Israel 1870); Montefiore's activity in the Land of Israel (Mishkenot Sha'ananim 1860); Baron Edmond de Rothschild ('Ha-Nadiv ha-Yadua') and the colonies; Baron Maurice de Hirsch and the Jewish Colonization Association (1891, Argentina); Hilfsverein (1901), the Joint (1914); philanthropy vs national solidarity; education systems; research-paper suggestion.

units.title: היהודים לאן? פתרונות לשאלת הקיום היהודי
units.scope: The 'Jewish question' at the end of the 19th century; solutions: Zionism – Hibbat Zion (Pinsker 'Auto-Emancipation' 1882, First Aliyah, Bilu), political Zionism (Herzl, 'Der Judenstaat' 1896, First Zionist Congress Basel 1897, Basel Program), spiritual/cultural Zionism (Ahad Ha'am), 'work in the present' (Gegenwartsarbeit, Helsingfors 1906); territorialism (the Uganda plan 1903, Zangwill's Jewish Territorial Organization 1905); emigration (mainly to the US); integration/assimilation; national minority in Eastern Europe: the Bund (1897, Yiddish, socialism, 'doikayt' – hereness), autonomism (Simon Dubnow); comparison table; structured debate with five groups and retrospective evaluation.
